title: Nature as an Adjunct to Digital Exposure: Effects of a Brief Nature-Based Intervention on Public Speaking Anxiety
summary:
Many people feel very anxious about speaking in front of others. An effective treatment is exposure therapy, in which people repeatedly face situations they fear. This study examines whether a short walk in nature can support a digital exposure intervention for public speaking anxiety. Two theories suggest why nature might help: natural surroundings may help restore the ability to direct attention and reduce mental fatigue, while time in nature may also reduce stress and tension. A brief walk may be an accessible, practical and low-cost addition to exposure.
Participants with fear of public speaking visit the laboratory on three days: Day 1, Day 4 and Day 9. At the first two visits, they give eight short speeches in front of a virtual audience. Halfway through the speeches, participants are assigned at random to take either an approximately 15-minute walk in a botanical garden or an urban virtual walk on a walking pad. At the third visit, they complete a speech test without another set of exposure speeches or a walk. Questionnaires, heart rate and skin conductance are used to assess anxiety across the visits. Participants also complete questionnaires about one week before the first visit and an online follow-up about one month after the third visit. The study also asks about participants’ expectations and satisfaction with the intervention.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Fluent German language skills
- Presence of public speaking anxiety (assessed by screening questions)
- Currently healthy, i.e. no current psychoatric disorders, except for Social Phobia, and not currently receiving psychotherapeutic treatment
Exclusion criteria:
Current mental disorder (except social phobia)
Cardiovascular or respiratory diseases
Neurological disorders
Current pregnancy
Participation in similar studies within the past 3 months
